# StrideBuddy

> StrideBuddy is a training diary app for track and field athletes. It runs on iPhone with iOS 18 or later. Athletes log reps, splits, races and strength work, get a weekly training plan and see race predictions.

StrideBuddy is a training diary, not a GPS running app. You enter the session you did: reps, splits, recoveries, race results and strength work. It does not import workouts from a watch, Strava or Garmin.

It is for adult athletes, 18 or older, who race on the track: sprinters, hurdlers, middle-distance and distance runners, and steeplechasers. It does not support jumps or throws.

Main features:

- Structured sessions with blocks, reps, splits and recoveries, including hurdles, steeplechase and hills
- Continuous runs, race results, strength work and Quick Notes
- Personal bests and training records. Hurdle reps have their own records, apart from flat reps
- A race calendar. Each race is marked A, B or C by how important it is
- Plan: a weekly training plan built with AI from your event, recent training, available days and races. Plan is in beta
- Race predictions made with AI, with a range and a confidence level. The first ones can appear after 5 logged sessions
- Weekly running volume for the last 12 weeks
- A free account (Sign in with Apple or Google) that syncs the diary across devices. The saved diary works offline

Price: StrideBuddy is in preview, and every feature is free during the preview. An account is required. Most features will stay free. A paid subscription for some AI features is planned for January 2027. AI features need an internet connection.

Platforms: an iPhone app for iOS 18 or later. A web app at https://web.stridebuddy.app uses the same account and shows the same diary.

Languages: English and Italian.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6760190939?pt=128627634&ct=website&mt=8

Support: support@stridebuddy.app

## Track tools

Free calculators and reference pages for track and field athletes. Each page shows the formula it uses, a worked example, its limits and its sources. Every tool is also in Italian: [Strumenti per l'atletica](https://stridebuddy.app/it/strumenti).

- [Track tools](https://stridebuddy.app/tools): All the tools on one page
- [Rep pace calculator](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/rep-pace): Type a session like 6x200 in 27-28 and get the pace per 100 m, 400 m and km, the total volume and the % of PB pace
- [Training paces from your PB](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/training-paces): A table of rep times at 60% to 120% of PB pace for common rep distances
- [Race time predictor](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/race-predictor): Race time estimates from 60 m to 10,000 m with the Riegel formula, from one PB or from two PBs
- [Race split planner](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/split-planner): Lap and cumulative splits for 400 m to 10,000 m on a 400 m or 200 m track, at even pace or with a chosen fade
- [Mile, 1500 m and 1600 m converter](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/mile-converter): Convert a time between the 1500 m, the mile and the 1600 m, and between the 3000 m, 2 miles and 3200 m
- [Hand time to FAT converter](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/hand-timing): Convert a hand time to a fully automatic time estimate and back, with the three conventions in use
- [Wind adjustment calculator](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/wind-adjustment): Still-air time estimates for the 100 m, 200 m and sprint hurdles, and whether the wind was legal for records
- [Decathlon and heptathlon points calculator](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/combined-events): Points per event and in total with the World Athletics scoring formulas, and the marks needed for a target score
- [Pace and unit converter](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/pace-converter): min/km, min/mile, per 400 m, km/h, mph and m/s, plus field-event marks in metres and feet and inches
- [Hurdle heights and spacings](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/hurdle-heights): Heights, number of hurdles and distances for every hurdle race and the steeplechase, by age group
- [Lane distances and staggers](https://stridebuddy.app/tools/lane-stagger): How far one lap is in each lane, and the staggers for the 200 m, 400 m, 800 m and relays
